augment

awg-MENT -- stress on the second syllable, MENT. · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To augment is to add to something to make it greater.

The hospital hired traveling nurses to augment its staff during the winter surge.

Example

A weekend tutor, two library books, and a nightly practice quiz augment the student's preparation, turning her shaky math grade into the strongest score on her report card.

Each one stacks extra resources on top of what she already had, making it greater. To augment is to add to something so that it grows in size, number, or strength.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

increase: To increase is the plain, all-purpose word for making something greater -- prices increase, and you can increase your effort. To augment is narrower and more purposeful: you add new resources onto something that already exists, building it up. Any augmenting is an increase, but increase says nothing about adding on.

boost: A boost is a quick push that lifts something for the moment -- a snack boosts your energy, a win boosts morale. To augment is slower and more lasting: you add real resources onto an existing base so it stays greater. A boost gives a shove; augmenting builds something up.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

diminish: to make smaller or less

reduce: to bring down in size or amount

Where it sits · how big the increase is

supplement → augment → amplify

supplement vs. augment: Supplement is more modest than augment -- a supplement tops something up with a little extra, while to augment is to build it up noticeably greater than before.

amplify vs. augment: Amplify is more dramatic than augment: augmenting a sound system adds more speakers, while amplifying the sound cranks its very intensity until it fills the hall.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — aug-: to increase (Latin augere)

suffix — -ment: result or means of (Latin -mentum)

Put it together: Augment comes from Latin augere, 'to increase' -- one of the great growth-roots of Latin. To augment something is simply to make it grow: you add to what already exists until it stands greater than before.

Use the root in a new word: auction: Half the town turned out for the auction, hoping to take home the old lighthouse clock.

Root Check

Word Choice

Augment takes a direct object: you augment your income, your skills, your forces, your vocabulary. It implies building on something that already exists -- you cannot augment what is not there yet -- and it is the polished choice where 'add to' would sound plain.
